newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Riksbank says Sweden to meet key EMU demands '97.
newsitem.headline: Riksbank says Sweden to meet key EMU demands '97.

text.p: Sweden's Riksbank (central bank) said on Wednesday the country would probably meet the Maastricht currency union requirements on inflation and interest rates next year.

"At the moment, Sweden has Europe's lowest (rate of) inflation and we expect Sweden to continue to fulfil the inflation criteria in 1997," Riksbank deputy governor Stefan Ingves told a conference on the European single currency.
"The recent downward tendency in interest rates indicates that we will probably also fulfill the interest rate criterion," Ingves added.

Ingves said inflation and interest rate targets were two criteria in the treaty that must be fulfilled by 1998 when the heads of state or government decide which countries to include in the currency union of the Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).

The currency stability criterion, which specifies that a currency must have participated in the Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM) for two years before the inception of the EMU, has been the source of heated debate in Sweden.
Some argue for a strict interpretation of the rules, while others argue that what counts in practice is the national currency's stability, Ingves said.
"Sweden adheres to the latter view," he said.
Regarding the remaining criteria, Ingves said Sweden's budget deficit for 1997 was expected to be close to the required three percent of GDP target specified in the treaty.
"The government has declared that it is prepared to implement measures if the deficit moves in an unfavourable direction," he said.
But he said it was not feasible to cut the government debt-to-GDP ratio, currently around 80 percent, to the stipulated 60 percent as early as 1997.
"However, the Maastricht Treaty provides for a flexible interpretation here," Ingves said.
"All-in-all, it therefore, looks as though we will fulfill the convergence criteria, which naturally makes it still more relevant, even for those who hesitated earlier, to begin the preparations."
